notes.meaning: The woman left her heavy water jar behind at the well and hurried back to town. She was so excited about what Jesus told her that ordinary chores no longer mattered. Her main concern was to bring others to hear him.

She invited the townspeople to come and see the man who knew her deepest secrets. She asked if he could be the Christ, which is God's promised Savior. She did not force her view on them, but stirred up their desire to meet him themselves.

The people immediately left the town and headed toward Jacob's well. Her honest words convinced them to check out Jesus for themselves. A whole crowd was soon streaming out along the road to find him.

While the woman was gone, the disciples begged Jesus to eat the food they had bought. They knew he was hot, tired, and hungry from traveling. They cared about his health, but Jesus had higher priorities in mind.

Jesus told his followers that he had food to eat that they knew nothing about. He was talking about the joy of leading people into God's kingdom. That spiritual work refreshed his soul far more than bread could.

The disciples wondered among themselves whether someone else had brought him a meal. They were still thinking only about physical food for the stomach. They often found it hard to see the deeper, spiritual meaning behind his words.

Jesus explained that his real food was doing the will of God his Father. Completing the work the Father gave him brought him total satisfaction and joy. Nothing on earth was more important to Jesus than saving lost souls.

Farmers usually had to wait four months between planting and harvest. Jesus pointed out that the spiritual harvest of souls was ready right now. The crowd of Samaritans walking across the fields showed that people were eager to hear God's truth.

The worker who gathers the harvest receives a reward and brings people into eternal life, which is living forever with God. Both the one who plants the seed and the one who reaps the crop share in the same great joy. In God's work, every helper celebrates the final outcome together.

Jesus repeated a common proverb saying that one person plants and another harvests. In daily life, this could be disappointing if a farmer never saw his crop. In God's kingdom, both workers share the victory and rejoice together.

Jesus sent his disciples to gather a harvest they had not prepared. Earlier prophets, teachers, and Jesus himself had already done the hard work of planting God's truth. Now the disciples had the privilege of seeing people accept the message.

Many Samaritans in that town came to believe in Jesus because of the woman's story. She openly admitted how Jesus exposed her past life. God used the honest words of an outcast woman to draw an entire community to Christ.

When the Samaritans met Jesus, they warmly asked him to stay with them. Even though Jews and Samaritans usually avoided each other, Jesus stayed there for two whole days. He welcomed the chance to teach them and build up their faith.

During those two days, many more people trusted in Jesus after listening to him speak. His own preaching had even greater power than the woman's report. When people hear God's word directly, their faith grows deep and strong.

The people told the woman that their faith no longer rested just on her words. They had heard Jesus for themselves and knew he truly was the Savior of the world. They realized his salvation was not only for Jews, but for all people everywhere.

After spending two days teaching in Samaria, Jesus continued his trip north into Galilee. He had set out for that region earlier and now resumed his journey. He went where God had planned for him to minister next.

Jesus himself had noted that a prophet does not receive honor in his own hometown. People who watch a prophet grow up often take him for granted and fail to respect him. Jesus knew what kind of reception lay ahead of him among his own people.

When Jesus arrived in Galilee, the locals welcomed him warmly. They had traveled to Jerusalem for the Passover festival and had seen the amazing miracles he did there. Their interest was stirred by the miracles, though they still needed deeper faith in his message.

Jesus returned to Cana in Galilee, the village where he had turned water into wine. Meanwhile, a royal official who served the ruler Herod had a son lying deathly sick in Capernaum. Sickness touches every family, even the rich and powerful.

When the official heard that Jesus was back in Galilee, he traveled about twenty miles to find him. He begged Jesus to come down to Capernaum and heal his dying boy. He had enough faith to ask for help, but thought Jesus had to be physically present in the room.

Jesus responded that the people would never believe unless they saw miraculous signs and wonders. He spoke this gentle challenge to the Galileans who demanded constant proof before trusting him. True faith takes God at his word without demanding spectacular sights first.

The desperate father did not argue with Jesus, but pleaded with him to hurry before the child died. He loved his son deeply and feared that time was running out. He did not yet realize that Jesus has power over death itself.

Jesus told the man to go home because his son would live. The official believed what Jesus said and set off on his journey without seeing any visible sign. His faith grew as he trusted the bare promise of Christ.

While the father was traveling down the road, his servants rushed out to meet him. They brought the joyful news that his boy was alive and well. God had answered his plea before he even reached his house.

The father asked his servants the exact time when the boy began to improve. They told him the fever broke yesterday at the seventh hour, which was one o'clock in the afternoon. The boy had not just slowly recovered, but was healed all at once.

The father realized that one o'clock was the very moment Jesus said the boy would live. This exact timing proved that the healing was a direct miracle from Jesus. As a result, the official and his entire family placed their full trust in Christ.

This was the second miraculous sign Jesus did in Galilee after coming from Judea. John highlights these two signs in Cana to show that Jesus has divine authority over nature and disease. They invite readers to believe that Jesus is the true Savior.
